title: Xploratory Future ideation
description: Initiated a futures research programme with the Royal College of Art to explore what mental health services could look like in 10-20 years, producing 33 scenarios and 10 user-tested product concepts.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: VP of Product & Innovation at Koa Health (Series B), in partnership with the Royal College of Art.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Product teams operating inside a company are constrained by near-term delivery. Roadmaps, quarterly targets, and user feedback loops all pull attention towards incremental improvement. For Koa Health, digital mental health was a fast-moving space with significant regulatory, clinical, and commercial uncertainty over a 10-20 year horizon. Without a structured view of where the space was heading, longer-term product strategy and investment decisions were being made on assumptions rather than evidence.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I initiated the programme, managed the RCA collaboration, and was responsible for connecting outputs back to strategic decisions within the company. Futures research and speculative design work was carried out by the RCA team; I provided the business framing and ensured the work was grounded in questions that mattered to the company.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Working with RCA researchers and designers, we ran a structured futures process combining horizon scanning, expert interviews, and speculative design. This produced 33 distinct future scenarios across technology, regulation, culture, and social behaviour. From these, we developed 10 future product concepts, which we then tested with target users online to assess desirability, perceived value, and concerns — giving the concepts empirical grounding and a basis for prioritisation.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• 33 future scenarios developed, covering a range of plausible mental health contexts over a 10-20 year horizon
  • 10 future product concepts tested with users online
  • Outputs published via the Xploratory website, contributing to Koa Health's positioning in the digital mental health space
  • Work directly informed longer-term product strategy and supported investor conversations about where the company was heading
